skills.name: Multiply matrices, including non-square ones, and use matrix equations

note.text:
Matrices can be multiplied when the number of columns of the first equals the number of rows of the second: (m × n)(n × p) gives an m × p matrix.
Each element of AB = (row of A) · (column of B): multiply in pairs and add.
Example: (1 2; 3 4)(5; 6) = (1×5 + 2×6; 3×5 + 4×6) = (17; 39).
Matrix multiplication is not commutative: usually AB ≠ BA.
A² means A × A. The identity I = (1 0; 0 1) has AI = IA = A.
In a matrix equation, equal matrices have equal elements in the same places.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text:
By the end, you should be able to multiply matrices of any compatible orders, explain why AB ≠ BA, and find unknowns in matrix equations.
Builds on: Form Three matrices: addition, scalar multiples and {2} × {2} products.
Leads to: Lesson {30} (determinants and inverses) and Lesson {31} (solving simultaneous equations with matrices).

sections.heading: When a product exists
sections.text:
A {2} × {3} matrix has {2} rows and {3} columns. To multiply A by B, each row of A must meet a column of B of the same length.
So: columns of A = rows of B. The answer takes the outside sizes:
• ({2} × {3})({3} × {1}) → {2} × {1}.  • ({1} × {2})({2} × {2}) → {1} × {2}.  • ({2} × {3})({2} × {3}): not possible.
Even when both AB and BA exist, they are usually different. Order matters.

key_words.meaning: able to be multiplied: columns of the first = rows of the second

mistake.why: Matrices are not multiplied element by element. Each answer element is a row times a column.

steps: The first matrix is {2} × {2}, the second {2} × {1}: the product is {2} × {1}.
Top: row ({a}, {b}) · column ({e}, {f}) = {a} × {e} + {b} × {f} = {a * e + b * f}.
Bottom: row ({c}, {d}) · column = {c} × {e} + {d} × {f} = {c * e + d * f}.

cards.idea: A product exists only when columns of the first = rows of the second; the answer has the outside sizes.
Each element of AB is a row of A times a column of B, multiplied in pairs and added.
Usually AB ≠ BA: the order matters.

distractors.text: {matStr([[a * e, b * f], [c * g, d * h]])}

misconceptions.explain: That is BA. The order matters: AB uses the rows of A.
Matrices are not multiplied element by element: row times column.

solution: Top left: {a} × {br(e)} + {b} × {br(g)} = {a * e + b * g}; top right: {a} × {br(f)} + {b} × {br(h)} = {a * f + b * h}.
Bottom: {c * e + d * g} and {c * f + d * h}.
where: matStr(matMul([[a, b], [c, d]], [[e, f], [g, h]])) != matStr(matMul([[e, f], [g, h]], [[a, b], [c, d]]))

questions.prompt: A is a {m} × {n} matrix and B is a {n} × {p} matrix. What is the order of AB?

misconceptions.explain: The matching inside numbers disappear: the answer has rows of A and columns of B.
Rows come from A ({m}), columns from B ({p}).
A has {n} columns and B has {n} rows, so the product exists.

solution: Columns of A ({n}) = rows of B ({n}), so AB exists.
Its order is the outside numbers: {m} × {p}.

questions.prompt: Find the element in row {i} and column {j} of AB.

misconceptions.explain: Multiply a whole row by a whole column and add, not just one pair.
Use a column of B, read downwards, not a row.

solution: Row {i} of A is ({i == 1 ? a : c}, {i == 1 ? b : d}); column {j} of B is ({j == 1 ? e : f}, {j == 1 ? g : h}).

distractors.text: {matStr([[a * e, b * f], [c * g, d * h]])}

misconceptions.explain: That is BA. The order matters: AB uses the rows of A.
Matrices are not multiplied element by element: row times column.

solution: Top left: {a} × {br(e)} + {b} × {br(g)} = {a * e + b * g}; top right: {a} × {br(f)} + {b} × {br(h)} = {a * f + b * h}.
Bottom: {c * e + d * g} and {c * f + d * h}.
where: matStr(matMul([[a, b], [c, d]], [[e, f], [g, h]])) != matStr(matMul([[e, f], [g, h]], [[a, b], [c, d]]))

questions.prompt: A = ({a}  {b} ; {c}  {d}). Find the top-left element of A².

misconceptions.explain: A² is not each element squared: top left is {a}² + {b} × {br(c)}.

solution: A² = A × A. Top left: row ({a}, {b}) · column ({a}, {c}).

misconceptions.wrong: (c * p + d * q - a * p) / q
misconceptions.explain: x is in the top row: use the top element.

solution: Top row: {a} × {p} + x × {q} = {a * p + x0 * q}.
